round: Code point restoration reseal of one lot 4 case (JS): idplan-007-utf16-key-order gets back the U+E000 occurrence key that separates UTF-16 code-unit order from code-point order
inputs: Spec-author audit of 2026-10-19 (lot 3 Unicode literal restoration, read-only audit of lots 4, 5 and X24): the U+E000 key of idplan-007 became the empty string in the derivation rework e054e0f, sealed in 3039d3a; with the keys (empty), U+10000, z, Z the UTF-16 and code-point orders give the same IDs, so the case no longer witnesses its derivation
First seal 2fdb505 of the case: requests U+E000, U+10000, z, Z; expected IDs Z e_0, z e_1, U+10000 e_2, U+E000 e_3

DESIGN R3.3 section 10.2 L801 (counter plan: domain order, then page.order and UTF-16 occurrenceKey), section 2.2 L126 (page order, then UTF-16 occurrenceKey), section 2.2 L130 (ordinary occurrence keys must be nonempty)
precedence: DESIGN R3.3 text > first-seal vector > later rewrite

idplan-007-utf16-key-order.defect: The seal fix round rewrite of the derivation helper (e054e0f) replaced the U+E000 occurrence key by the empty string. The sealed vector (empty), U+10000, z, Z sorts identically under UTF-16 code units, code points and UTF-8 bytes, so a code-point implementation passed the case its derivation says it rejects; the empty key with domain node also contradicted DESIGN L130.
idplan-007-utf16-key-order.decision: Restore the first-seal key U+E000 at the same request position, written as the braced escape \u{E000} in the ASCII derivation source. L801 allocates in UTF-16 occurrenceKey order: Z (005A), z (007A), U+10000 (D800 DC00), U+E000 (E000).

derivation.old: Occurrence keys sort by UTF-16 code units: Z (0x5A), z (0x7A), U+10000 (surrogate 0xD800) and then U+E000; code-point order would place U+E000 before U+10000.
derivation.new: Four nonempty node keys of page P, requested as U+E000, U+10000, z, Z, sort by UTF-16 code units: Z (0x005A) e_0, z (0x007A) e_1, U+10000 (surrogate pair 0xD800 0xDC00) e_2, then U+E000 (0xE000) e_3. Code-point order would place U+E000 (e_2) before U+10000 (e_3).

wrongImplementation.old: Code-point or locale collation of occurrence keys.
wrongImplementation.new: Code-point or UTF-8 byte order of occurrence keys (U+E000 e_2, U+10000 e_3), locale collation (z before Z), or numbering in request order (U+E000 e_0).

discrimination.note: IDs that differ from the sealed allocation under each named wrong key order (models, not implementations); locale-en is the default collation of locale en.

untouched: The clause list (10.2 L801, 2.2 L126), the design excerpts, the docs clause table and every other case, artifact and index entry are unchanged.
method: Targeted reseal. The derivation source writes the restored key as \u{E000}; a standalone Node stdlib helper (no import from src/, dist/ or the derive/ tool) rebuilt the old case bytes from a hand table to validate its model, then derived the new allocation from hand UTF-16 code-unit tables, wrote the case file, the two index strings, the README row, the manifest digest and the five seal entries, and read every written file back byte for byte. A separate in-memory replay of the authored part of the derivation tool (no vendor step, no write) reproduces the 197 authored case files, their artifacts, index entries, README rows and manifest digests of the sealed tree. No loader, compiler, evaluator, layout or exporter of the implementation was run or imported.
testChange: tests/profile-lot4-seal.test.mjs: the ledger chain test reads the micro-fix ledger as history (successor = micro-fix seal) and binds this ledger to the current bytes; a new test checks that the idplan-007 case and its derivation source keep U+E000 (UTF-8 EE 80 80 in the request list and in the expected IDs, braced escape in the source), that its keys are nonempty, and that code-point order, UTF-8 byte order, case-folded order and request order each give other IDs than the sealed UTF-16 allocation. Test count 20 to 21.
